description: This circular chart visually organizes and categorizes key principles and duties in medical ethics, structured around three primary domains: Justice, Non-Maleficence, and Autonomy, each represented by a distinct colored segment. The chart is divided into 18 labeled slices, with the largest segment being “Justice” in orange, followed by “Autonomy” in green, and “Non-Maleficence” in purple. The “Justice” category contains six sub-principles, including “Promote Environmental Sustainability,” “Allocate Medical Sources Fairly,” and “Prevent Patient from Harm.” The “Autonomy” category includes nine sub-principles such as “Physician Can Freely Choose Whom to Serve,” “Make Responsible and Independent Clinical Judgement,” and “Respect Patient’s Rights to be Informed/Freedom of Choice.” The “Non-Maleficence” category contains three sub-principles: “Maintain Qualified When Providing Medical Care,” “Report Unethical and Unprofessional Conduct,” and “Do Not Use Medicine for Personal Gain.” The remaining nine sub-principles are grouped under the “Justice” and “Autonomy” categories, with “Provide Medical Care to Patients,” “Continual Learning,” and “Respect and Cooperate with Colleagues” falling under “Justice,” while “Respect Life, Dignity of Patients,” “Give Top Priority to Patient’s Interest in Conflict of Interests,” and “Minimizing Conflicts of Interest” are under “Autonomy.” The chart does not include percentage labels or a legend, and all slices are presented in a radial, descending order of size, with no visual emphasis or explosion applied to any segment.
